thread.title: The FAANG Stocks Lost More Than $140 Billion in Value

title: The FAANG Stocks Lost More Than $140 Billion in Value
text:
Amazon Got Beat Down on a Bad Day for the Big Tech Stocks. Here’s How Much They Lost. By Updated Dec. 5, 2018 5:45 a.m. ET Order Reprints Photograph by Guillaume Souvant/AFP/Getty Images Text size
It was an ugly Tuesday for popular technology stocks.
The so-called FAANG basket of tech giants lost more than $140 billion in stock value during the day’s trading session.
FAANG stocks are a basket of high-growth technology names: Facebook (FB), Amazon.com (AMZN), Apple (AAPL), Netflix (NFLX) and Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL).
Amazon stock led the list of decliners with a loss of $51 billion in stock value. The company’s shares declined about 6% after a government task force appointed by President Donald Trump recommended the U.S. Postal Service price commercial use of package delivery services “with the intent of optimizing revenue.” FAANG Stocks' Decline in Value On Dec. 4, 2018
In October, Jefferies analyst Brent Thill estimated a proposed 2019 postal rate increase will add roughly $700 million in expenses for Amazon.
Apple stock was the second largest loser with a fall of $39 billion in market value.
On Monday, HSBC Global Research downgraded Apple stock to Hold from Buy , citing the market saturation in the global smartphone market.
Cirrus Logic (CRUS), a maker of audio chips for the iPhone, also reduced its financial guidance for its third quarter on Monday, citing “recent weaknesses in the smartphone market.” In its most recent annual filing, Cirrus Logic said Apple accounted for 81% of its sales in its fiscal 2018. Netflix stock also declined 5.2%, losing $6.5 billion in stock value, after the New York Times reported the video streaming company will pay WarnerMedia about $100 million for the right to stream Friends in 2019, citing people with direct knowledge of the matter. The fee is up from the $30 million a year the company paid previously.
The company’s skeptics have worried about the rising costs of content and its financial position. Netflix has burned through $2.2 billion in cash over its previous four quarters. As of the end of the third quarter, it had long-term debt of $8.3 billion and $18.6 billion of content obligations.
The total stock value lost from FAANG stocks on Tuesday was $142.5 billion.
